A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original persona-steering, localization, and ablation experiments, plus human–LLM judgment agreement results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and reports additional random-head, cosine-score, general-text control, and architecture-specific analyses.

M1.justification: Difference-in-means extraction, geometric localization, the dot-product Head Contribution Score, and activation addition to selected heads are retained. Cosine similarity is tested as a supplementary check, without replacing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds OpenAssistant responses as general-text control data. The six persona tasks and general-utility evaluations remain unchanged. Gemma and Qwen3-MoE analyses were already mentioned in v1 Appendix F.

E2.justification: v2 adds random-head ablation as an evaluated comparator to targeted-head ablation for Qwen2.5-7B in Appendix D.2.1. The five steering-site comparators in Section 5 and Table 1 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New control protocols include averaging responses to 1,000 OpenAssistant questions, random ablation across head counts, and cosine-based reassessment of head contributions. Figure 2 extends some Qwen coefficient sweeps to -4 through 4. The main sample counts, judge, decoding settings, and Tables 11–12 configurations are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices D.2 and D.4 add substantial checks of head specificity, sensitivity to vector norms, and persona-specific versus generic representation transitions. Appendix F supplies detailed layer/head steering and heatmap analyses for Gemma and Qwen3-MoE, expanding v1's brief preliminary architecture observations.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over five independent runs in Section 2.4. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 13 substantially revises lower-envelope results and no longer duplicates the two model blocks; Qwen Head Cor hallucination under Neg+Add changes from 25.6 to 59.8. Figure 2 and coherency Pareto curves also change, and new control and architecture results are reported. The Llama per-head coherency panel in v1 Figure 11c is removed. Table 1 and human-agreement tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and Definition 5.1 are retained. The added cosine and hidden-state comparisons are empirical analyses, without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: asymmetric coherency degradation, geometrically identifiable Style Modulation Heads, and improved steering through localized intervention. The new conclusion restates these claims and their previously discussed implications.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the mechanistic discussion by addressing vector-norm and generic-processing explanations and interpreting distributed localization in larger models through capacity. Section 7 adds limitations concerning combination with other steering strategies and intervention granularity, while removing v1's persona-diversity and post-training caveat.

D1.justification: v2 specifies gemma-3-12b-it and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, documents OpenAssistant averaging, and acknowledges Azure/Miyabi computing resources. Its own code link and steering-configuration tables remain unchanged; the direct Persona Vectors repository reference is replaced by a paper citation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Koishekenov et al. (2026) for the alternative processing-phase explanation and Köpf et al. (2023) for OpenAssistant. The central positioning around where, how, and when to steer remains intact. Most other citation changes update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: Most existing scientific prose is retained. v2 introduces separate limitations and conclusion sections, reorganizes Appendices D and F, and updates affiliations, acknowledgments, publication information, and bibliography formatting.

P2.justification: Figures 3–4 combine Qwen results with former Llama appendix panels, changing the main visual organization. New multipanel control and architecture figures substantially expand the displays. Axes, captions, and figure placement are revised, and the Llama per-head coherency panel is omitted.

improvement.justification: The new controls in Appendices D.2 and D.4 directly test important alternative explanations left untested in v1, strengthening the central specialization argument. Appendix F makes previously brief architecture observations inspectable, and Table 13 replaces duplicated model values. These gains substantially improve empirical support and assessment of applicability. Removing the persona-diversity caveat and Llama per-head coherency panel causes smaller losses.
